metadata.title: A short proof of Brooks' theorem

nodes.name: PathColor procedure
nodes.statement: For an uncolored path $P=v_1v_2\dots v_j$ in a graph $G$ with $\Delta(G)\leq k$ partially $k$-colored, $\mathrm{PathColor}(v_1,\dots,v_{j-1};v_j)$ colors $v_1,\dots,v_{j-1}$ consecutively along $P$, leaving $v_j$ uncolored.
nodes.statement_clean: Sequential greedy coloring procedure for a path that leaves the last vertex uncolored.

nodes.name: List coloring
nodes.statement: Given a list $L(v)$ of $k$ admissible colors for each vertex $v$ of $G$, a list coloring of $G$ is a proper coloring in which the color of each vertex is chosen from its list.

nodes.name: Constraint graph (correspondence coloring)
nodes.statement: For a graph $G$ and list assignment $L$, the constraint graph $F=F(L,G)$ has vertex set $\{(v,a):v\in V(G),\,a\in L(v)\}$; for each edge $uv\in E(G)$ fix an arbitrary partial matching between $\{u\}\times L(u)$ and $\{v\}\times L(v)$; no other edges exist in $F$.

nodes.name: Coloring respecting $F$
nodes.statement: A coloring $c$ of $G$ from lists $L(v)$ respects $F$ if $(u,c(u))$ and $(v,c(v))$ are never adjacent in $F$.

nodes.name: Signed graph proper coloring
nodes.statement: A signed graph is a graph $G$ whose edges are labeled by $\{+,-\}$. A vertex coloring $c$ by real numbers is proper if for every adjacent $u,v$: $c(u)+c(v)\neq 0$ or $c(u)-c(v)\neq 0$, according to the label of edge $uv$.

nodes.name: Brooks' theorem
nodes.statement: Let $k\geq 3$ be a natural number. Let $G$ be a graph with $\Delta(G)\leq k$. If $G$ does not contain a clique on $k+1$ vertices, then $G$ is $k$-colorable.
assumptions: $G$ does not contain a clique on $k+1$ vertices

nodes.name: Brooks-type theorem for correspondence coloring
nodes.statement: Let $k\geq 3$ and let $G$ be a graph with $\Delta(G)\leq k$ not containing a clique on $k+1$ vertices. For any list assignment $L$ with $|L(v)|=k$ and any constraint graph $F$ for $(L,G)$, there exists a list coloring of $G$ respecting $F$.
assumptions: $G$ does not contain a clique on $k+1$ vertices
$L$ is a list assignment with $|L(v)|=k$ for all $v$
$F$ is an arbitrary constraint graph for $(L,G)$
conclusions: There exists a list coloring of $G$ respecting $F$

nodes.name: PathColor observation
nodes.statement: If $G$ is partially $k$-colored with $\Delta(G)\leq k$, then along any uncolored path $P=v_1\dots v_j$ each vertex $v_i$ ($i<j$) can be greedily colored because its successor $v_{i+1}$ is still uncolored; $\mathrm{PathColor}$ does nothing if $j=1$.

nodes.name: Proof of Brooks' theorem
nodes.statement: Induction on $|V(G)|=n$; reduce to $G$ $k$-regular, pick non-adjacent neighbors $x,y$ of a vertex $v$, extend a maximal path $P=v_1v_2v_3\dots v_r$ with $v_1=x,v_2=v,v_3=y$; split into Case 1 ($r=n$) and Case 2 ($r<n$).

nodes.name: Base case and reduction to $k$-regular
nodes.statement: Induct on $n=|V(G)|$. For $n\leq k$ the claim is trivial. If $G$ has a vertex of degree $<k$, delete it and apply induction; thus assume $G$ is $k$-regular.

nodes.name: Choose non-adjacent neighbors and build maximal path
nodes.statement: Pick any vertex $v$. Since $G$ has no clique on $k+1$ vertices, two neighbors $x,y$ of $v$ are non-adjacent. Set $v_1=x,v_2=v,v_3=y$ and extend $P=v_1v_2v_3\dots v_r$ until some $v_r$ has all neighbors on $P$.

nodes.name: Case split on $r=n$ vs $r<n$
nodes.statement: Distinguish Case 1 where the maximal path covers all vertices ($r=n$) from Case 2 where some vertices remain ($r<n$).

nodes.name: Case 1: $r=n$
nodes.statement: Let $v_j$ be a neighbor of $v_2$ other than $v_1,v_3$ (exists since $k\geq 3$). Color $v_1,v_3$ the same; apply $\mathrm{PathColor}(v_4,\dots,v_{j-1};v_j)$ and $\mathrm{PathColor}(v_n,v_{n-1},\dots,v_j;v_2)$; finally color $v_2$, possible because two of its neighbors share a color.

nodes.name: Case 2: $r<n$ — extract cycle $C$ and color $G'$
nodes.statement: Let $v_j$ be the smallest-index neighbor of $v_r$, so $C=v_jv_{j+1}\dots v_r$ is a cycle. Set $G'=G-C$ and color it by induction. If no edge between $G'$ and $C$, induct on $C$ separately and finish.

nodes.name: Case 2: bridge from $G'$ to $C$ and finish coloring
nodes.statement: If some $v_l\in C$ has neighbor $u\in G'$ (take largest such index $l<r$), give $v_{l+1}$ the color of $u$; apply $\mathrm{PathColor}(v_{l+2},\dots,v_r,v_j,\dots,v_{l-1};v_l)$, then color $v_l$, since two of its neighbors share a color.

nodes.name: DFS-based Brooks coloring algorithm
nodes.statement: Iterative DFS-based $k$-coloring algorithm derived from the inductive proof of Brooks' theorem, running in $O(m+n)$ time.
input: Integer $k\geq 3$ with $\Delta(G)\leq k$ and $G$ contains no clique on $k+1$ vertices
nodes.pseudocode:
1. Choose root $v$ (preferably with $\deg(v)<k$ when available); build a DFS tree.
2. Run DFS labeling all vertices.
3. Greedily color vertices in order of decreasing DFS labels using $\mathrm{PathColor}$ along discovered paths.
4. In Case 2, color $v_n,v_{n-1},\dots,v_{r+1}$ and $v_1,\dots,v_{j-1}$ before coloring the back-edge cycle $C$.
5. If $\deg(v_r)=1$, treat $C=K_2$ trivially or restart DFS at $v_r$.

nodes.name: Build DFS tree from chosen root
nodes.statement: Pick a root $v$ — preferably a vertex with $\deg(v)<k$ if one exists — and run DFS to label all vertices.

nodes.name: Greedy coloring in decreasing DFS-label order
nodes.statement: Process vertices in order of decreasing DFS labels and greedily assign a color from the $k$ available, emulating the inductive argument.

nodes.name: Handle Case 2 cycle without invoking induction
nodes.statement: Color $v_n,v_{n-1},\dots,v_{r+1}$ and $v_1,\dots,v_{j-1}$ greedily; then color the back-edge cycle $C$ using the same scheme as in the proof.

nodes.name: Handle degenerate $\deg(v_r)=1$ case
nodes.statement: If $\deg(v_r)=1$ then $C=K_2$; the last part of the proof works trivially since $\mathrm{PathColor}$ colors zero vertices, or alternatively restart DFS with $v_r$ as the root.

nodes.name: Linear-time complexity comparison
nodes.statement: Using Skulrattanakulchai's data structure (proof of Theorem 12 in [Sku]), the present algorithm runs in $O(m+n)$ time, comparable to but conceptually simpler than the algorithm in [Sku] — no biconnected components or special subgraphs required.

nodes.name: Signed graphs as special case
nodes.statement: Theorem 2 covers a Brooks-type result for signed graphs as a special case of correspondence coloring, extending results of [MacajovaRS], [FleinerWiener], [Stiebitz].
